test_title: PYST 34: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 20 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Rodney has two grandsons Amit and Gopal. 11 year old Amit gets some money from Rodney's wealth and 12 year old Gopal gets rest of the money. But Amit and Gopal will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 10% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Rodney given Gopal (in ₹) initially, if total money with Rodney was ₹23100 ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in time invested = 12 − 11 = 1 year.

For equal amounts at compound interest, the ratio of their principals (Gopal : Amit) = (1 + R/100)Time Diff : 1

Gopal : Amit = (1 + 10/100)¹ : 1 = 11/10 : 1 = 11 : 10

Total parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts ⇒ 21 parts = 23100

1 part = 23100 ÷ 21 = 1100

Gopal's share = 11 parts = 11 × 1100 = 12100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money = ₹23100

Age of Amit = 11 years | Age of Gopal = 12 years.

They receive the money when they turn 23 years old.

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually.

**Formula Used:**

Amount in CI, A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ
